description: windows.yml's native pytest steps (artifact storage and reparse portability, the Windows compatibility seams, and the bootstrap harness), each writing its own build/skip-report-windows-*.json and gated on it. Classified from Windows run 36898564289 on cf28fe7 (2026-10-01), whose one recorded skip was the POSIX process-group case, and from each selected file's os.name skip conditions. Its macOS coverage names macos-hosted, the runner macos.yml reports as since Stage 38 (CL-R-36), so every claim is checked against hosted reports on each push; the acceptance Mac runs a superset.

rules.note: test_stage_timeout_kills_spawned_descendants kills a POSIX process group; Windows has none. The macOS and Linux btrc shards run it.
Windows sets artifact times through the handle API instead, which the native Windows cases of the same file prove here.
Windows has no mkfifo; the special-file rejection runs on the POSIX unit shards.
CX-UIA-09 shell requires its host provider; both frontends and sanitizer modes run on the named stand-in.
The real X11 and Wayland desktop check (CL-UIA-11) runs only on a physical Linux desktop, PLAN D7's host; the devcontainer skips it as awaiting hardware, so it is not covered there.
CX-UIA-09 shell requires its host provider; both frontends and sanitizer modes run on the named stand-in.
The patched SDL's X11 clipboard path (nix/sdl3-x11-selection-requestor.patch) exists only on Linux; the probe runs under the Linux virtual display.

rules.reason: ^Android activity lifecycle simulation requires POSIX fork$
rules.note: The lifecycle simulator compiles the Android C host and executes its POSIX fork/thread/file path. It is a local lifetime regression, not Android emulator qualification.
Real Linux ProcessThreads directory-read failure and closure, paired plain/sanitized native fixture.

rules.reason: ^Library\.Network has providers for Linux and macOS only$
rules.note: TCPStream and TCPListener have BSD-socket rows for Linux and macOS; test_windows_has_no_network_provider_yet runs here and pins the refusal. The macOS and Linux shards run the loopback conformance.

rules.reason: ^Library\.USB carries transfers over Library\.Network, which has Linux and macOS rows only$
rules.note: USB/IP runs over TCPStream; test_windows_builds_usb_values_but_no_transport runs here and pins what does build. The macOS and Linux shards run the emulated device.

rules.reason: ^requires Linux: Library\.Crypto's libsodium provider has a Linux row only$
rules.note: Sodium has a libsodium provider on Linux only; test_windows_builds_base64_but_no_keys runs on every host and pins what builds without one. The Linux shard runs the signatures, key files and the channel.
